evidence: Read cold in CONTEXT.txt: the draft is the last sentence of the paragraph that begins "When I do it on my own, I can detect when the wording I'm using ..." and appears once, verbatim: "I can tell when my body is saying no, before my conscious mind can twist it around to a yes." It follows "When I use an image, I can tell whether it's giving me useful information, or just telling me what I'm afraid of, ..." as the paragraph's third thing he can do on his own, so it needs no "And" and nothing arrives unprepared. CHANGE: it is Emulate's one sentence (the_change describes it as the body's no noticed before the conscious mind can twist it into a yes; the draft's "twist it around to a yes" is the same thing). PRONOUN: "it" in "twist it around" is the no, the body's "no" that opens the sentence; the other noun it could grammatically take ("my body") cannot be twisted to a yes, so it resolves at once (C02 clear). MEANING vs SOURCE.txt: the words replaced are "And I can notice my body saying no before my conscious mind talks me into a yes" and his published line is "I can catch the body's no before the conscious mind writes a persuasive little essay called yes". Kept: he can catch the body's no early, before the conscious mind turns it into a yes. "I can tell when" = "I can notice/catch"; "before my conscious mind can ..." keeps the timing. One real shift, judged small: persuasion ("talks me into", "persuasive little essay") becomes distortion ("twist it around to"), but both name the conscious mind rationalizing the body's no into a yes, and the job of the line is intact; no new claim and no new fact (C03 and C04 absent). TELLS: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 and find none PRESENT. Nearest calls: T20/T17 (the paragraph ends on a no/yes antithesis) are not present because the line adds a new, separate thing he can do rather than summing up the paragraph (so not T29 either), the antithesis is the source's own content (his published line is more flourished than this plain version), and the run of short paragraph endings stops at two ("trust and precision", then this line) before a long parenthetical; T26 is not present: "I can tell" now sits in two consecutive sentences ("I can tell whether ... I can tell when") with "telling" between them, but it is an ordinary phrase used as a deliberate parallel for one skill applied to wording, images and the body, and the replaced "I can notice" had the same "I can" frame; T15 is not present: the swaps ("notice" to "tell when", "talks me into" to "twist it around to") are plain common idioms, not rarer words, and the clause is reshaped; T16/T18 absent (no "not X, it's Y" and no short flip sentence; the no/yes contrast sits inside one sentence); T12 absent (the one contrast is the point of the sentence, not a tidy pair); T07 absent (no filler); T06 absent (concrete, and his own concept of the body's no). Cosmetic only: the tell/telling/tell echo and "to a yes" are slightly loose but read as casual speech. LINTER: one finding, "D9 follows the source order", accepted: it is a single sentence carrying one point, so there is no order to disturb; the surrounding paragraph's order is unchanged, and the sentence notices a real contrast (no versus yes) that is its content, so T13 and T09 are clear. Note on the writer's ledger: its T14 and T15 evidence says this sentence puts back the author's point or words, but the_change records no such fix here (the sentence is Emulate's as is), so I judged T14 and T15 on the draft itself.
